newsitem.title: USA: BP, Fina approve Alaska oil field project.
newsitem.headline: BP, Fina approve Alaska oil field project.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc unit BP Exploration Alaska Inc and PetroFina S.A. (Fina) on Thursday approved the development of the Badami oil field about 35 miles east of Prudhoe Bay in Alaska, BP said.

Development of the field will cost about $300 million, with the first oil slated to pump in late 1998. Gravel placement for production facilities and wells is underway, and output is expected to peak at 35,000 barrels-per-day in 1999, BP said in a statement.
Badami contains an estimated 120 million barrels of recoverable oil, making it the ninth-largest among 13 North Slope fields now producing oil or slated for development, the company said.

While about two-thirds of the recoverable reserves are offshore, Badami will be developed from a single onshore location, using directional drilling. Drilling is scheduled to begin in the third quarter, the company said.
The field was discovered in 1990 by Conoco Inc., a unit of Dupont Co, and Fina. BP joined the project in 1992 and acquired Conoco's remaining interest in Badami in 1993.
BP operates the field and has a 70 percent interest. PetroFina S.A., of Belgium, owns the remaining 30 percent, which is managed by Fina Inc., its U.S. affiliate.
